issues.issue: Should the OS GPS device be removed and the BI GPS device reinstalled?
issues.applicant_position: OS device is heavier, thicker and needs daily charging; it causes a rash and sleep disruption, unlike the BI device.
issues.respondent_position: Jaballah has not shown he is entitled to the relief; CBSA's switch to the OS device was not excessive treatment.
issues.result_quote: It follows that the OS GPS device should be removed and be replaced with a BI GPS device.

issues.issue: Must the Court decide the Charter challenge (sections 7 and 12) to resolve the motion?
issues.applicant_position: Liberty and security interests under section 7 are engaged and infringed; over time the treatment may become cruel and unusual under section 12.
issues.respondent_position: Accepts section 7 is engaged but says no principle of fundamental justice is breached and the treatment is not excessive.
issues.result_quote: While the parties frame this motion in terms of the Charter, I do not find it necessary to resort to the Charter in order to adjudicate upon the motion.

issues.issue: Can the Court vary its earlier release-conditions order for matters that arose after it was made?
issues.applicant_position: Court can vary the order under Rule 399(2) because the device difficulties arose after the conditions order was made.
issues.respondent_position: Acknowledged the Court's Rule 399(2) power at oral argument; disputed that Jaballah is entitled to the relief sought.
issues.result_quote: matters that arose or were drawn to the Court's attention subsequent to the making of the order
